member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.DSP.DSPConst.DefaultSampleSize
member.summary: Used by DSP Filters to Set the default Split Size. This is needed when a large Buffer arrives and the Application would't respond until the DSP is done. If the SampleSize of an Filter is Set to Value > 0 then the Buffer will be splitted at this amount of Samples and processed until all Samples are processed. After every Process, Application.ProcessMessages is called to make the Application respond to Windows. DefaultSampleSize is just a default Value. The SampleSize can be changed on every Filter seperate.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.DSP.DSPConverter
member.summary: Static methods to convert between different sample formats.

remarks.para: Code is mainly based on information available on the original C source code pa_converters.c from Portable Audio I/O Library.
This class try to be as fast as possible without using unsafe code.
Dither isn't currently supported. Currently supported conversions are 'to' and 'from' conversions between the following value types:
Integer 8-bit (byte), Integer 16-bit (Int16), Integer 32-bit (Int32), Single precision 32-bit floating point (float).
Which are the most common PCM formats.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.GenICam.AlliedVision.VimbaAPI.VmbFeaturesList(System.IntPtr,System.IntPtr,System.UInt32,System.UInt32@,System.UInt32)
member.summary: Lists all the features for this entity.
member.remarks: This function lists all implemented features, whether they are currently available or not. The list of features does not change as long as the entity is connected. This function is usually called twice: once with an empty list to query the length of the list, and then again with a list of the correct length. If VmbErrorMoreData is returned and numFound is non-null, the total number of features has been written to numFound. If there are more elements in featureInfoList than features available, the remaining elements are filled with zero-initialized VmbFeatureInfo_t structs.
member.param: Handle for an entity that exposes features.
An array of VmbFeatureInfo_t to be filled by the API. May be null if numFound is used for size query.
Number of VmbFeatureInfo_t elements found. May be null if featureInfoList is not null.
member.returns: An error code indicating success or the type of error that occurred.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.GStreamer.DSP.DSPConverter
member.summary: Static methods to convert between different sample formats.

remarks.para: Code is mainly based on information available on the original C source code pa_converters.c from Portable Audio I/O Library.
This class try to be as fast as possible without using unsafe code.
Dither isn't currently supported. Currently supported conversions are 'to' and 'from' conversions between the following value types:
Integer 8-bit (byte), Integer 16-bit (Int16), Integer 32-bit (Int32), Single precision 32-bit floating point (float).
Which are the most common PCM formats.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1
member.summary:
Circular buffer.
When writing to a full buffer: PushBack -> removes this[0] / Front() PushFront -> removes this[Size-1] / Back()
this implementation is inspired by http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/libs/circular_buffer/doc/circular_buffer.html because I liked their interface.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1._start
member.summary: The _start. Index of the first element in buffer.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1._end
member.summary: The _end. Index after the last element in the buffer.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.#ctor(System.Int32)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.#ctor(System.Int32,`0[])
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.param: Items to fill buffer with. Items length must be less than capacity. Suggestion: use Skip(x).Take(y).ToArray() to build this argument from any enumerable.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.Capacity
member.summary: Maximum capacity of the buffer. Elements pushed into the buffer after maximum capacity is reached (IsFull = true), will remove an element.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.IsFull
member.summary: Boolean indicating if Circular is at full capacity. Adding more elements when the buffer is full will cause elements to be removed from the other end of the buffer.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.Size
member.summary: Current buffer size (the number of elements that the buffer has).

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.Front
member.summary: Element at the front of the buffer - this[0].
member.returns: The value of the element of type T at the front of the buffer.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.Back
member.summary: Element at the back of the buffer - this[Size - 1].
member.returns: The value of the element of type T at the back of the buffer.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.Item(System.Int32)
member.summary: Index access to elements in buffer. Index does not loop around like when adding elements, valid interval is [0;Size[
member.exception: Thrown when index is outside of [; Size[ interval.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.PushBack(`0)
member.summary:
Pushes a new element to the back of the buffer. Back()/this[Size-1] will now return this element.
When the buffer is full, the element at Front()/this[0] will be popped to allow for this new element to fit.
member.param: Item to push to the back of the buffer

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.PushFront(`0)
member.summary:
Pushes a new element to the front of the buffer. Front()/this[0] will now return this element.
When the buffer is full, the element at Back()/this[Size-1] will be popped to allow for this new element to fit.
member.param: Item to push to the front of the buffer

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.PopBack
member.summary: Removes the element at the back of the buffer. Decreasing the Buffer size by 1.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.PopFront
member.summary: Removes the element at the front of the buffer. Decreasing the Buffer size by 1.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.Clear
member.summary: Clears the contents of the array. Size = 0, Capacity is unchanged.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.ToArray
member.summary: Copies the buffer contents to an array, according to the logical contents of the buffer (i.e. independent of the internal order/contents)
member.returns: A new array with a copy of the buffer contents.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.ToArraySegments
member.summary:
Get the contents of the buffer as 2 ArraySegments. Respects the logical contents of the buffer, where each segment and items in each segment are ordered according to insertion.
Fast: does not copy the array elements. Useful for methods like Send(IList<ArraySegment<Byte>>).
Segments may be empty.
member.returns: An IList with 2 segments corresponding to the buffer content.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Helpers.CircularBuffer`1.GetEnumerator
member.summary: Returns an enumerator that iterates through this buffer.
member.returns: An enumerator that can be used to iterate this collection.

member.summary: Increments the provided index variable by one, wrapping around if necessary.

member.summary: Decrements the provided index variable by one, wrapping around if necessary.

We need a bit of work to ensure that exceptions are appropriately propagated, as the exception is generated at type initialization time, but we wish it to be thrown as an ArgumentException. Note that this type we do not have a constructor constraint on TTarget, because we only use the constructor when we use the form which creates a new instance.

member.summary: List of properties to grab values from. The corresponding targetProperties list contains the same properties in the target type. Unfortunately we can't use expression trees to do this, because we basically need a sequence of statements. We could build a DynamicMethod, but that's significantly more work :) Please mail me if you really need this...

member.summary: Gets or sets the tag types contained in the current instance.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Title
member.summary: Gets or sets the title for the media described by the current instance.
member.remarks: The title is most commonly the name of the song or episode or a movie title. For example, "Daydream Believer" (a song by the Monkies), "Space Seed" (an episode of Star Trek), or "Harold and Kumar Go To White Castle" (a movie).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Performers
member.summary: Gets or sets the performers or artists who performed in the media described by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the performers or artists who performed in the media described by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field is most commonly called "Artists" in media applications and should be used to represent each of the artists appearing in the media. It can be simple in theform of "The Beatles", or more complicated in the form of "John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, Pete Best", depending on the preferences of the listener and the degree to which they organize their media collection.
As the preference of the user may vary, applications should not try to limit the user in what choice they may make.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.AlbumArtists
member.summary: Gets or sets the band or artist who is credited in the creation of the entire album or collection containing the media described by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the band or artist who is credited in the creation of the entire album or collection containing the media described by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field is typically optional but aids in the sorting of compilations or albums with multiple artists. For example, if an album has several artists, sorting by artist will split up the album and sorting by album will split up albums by the same artist. Having a single album artist for an entire album will solve this problem.

As this value is to be used as a sorting key, it should be used with less variation than . Where performers can be broken into muliple artist it is best to stick with a single band name. For example, "The Beatles".

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Composers
member.summary: Gets or sets the composers of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the composers of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the composers, song writers, script writers, or persons who claim authorship of the media.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Album
member.summary: Gets or sets the album of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A object containing the album of the media represented by the current instance or if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the name of the album the media belongs to. In the case of a boxed set, it should be the name of the entire set rather than the individual disc.
For example, "Rubber Soul" (an album by the Beatles), "The Sopranos: Complete First Season" (a boxed set of TV episodes), or "Back To The Future Trilogy" (a boxed set of movies).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Comment
member.summary: Gets or sets a user comment on the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A object containing user comments on the media represented by the current instance or if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field should be used to store user notes and comments. There is no constraint on what text can be stored here, but it should not contain program information.

Because this field contains notes that the user might think of while listening to the media, it may be useful for an application to make this field easily accessible, perhaps even including it in the main interface.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Genres
member.summary: Gets or sets the genres of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the genres of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Year
member.summary: Gets or sets the year that the media represented by the current instance was recorded.
member.value: A containing the year that the media represented by the current instance was created or zero if no value is present.

remarks.para: Years greater than 9999 cannot be stored by most tagging formats and will be cleared if a higher value is set.
Some tagging formats store higher precision dates which will be truncated when this property is set. Format specific implementations are necessary access the higher precision values.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Track
member.summary: Gets or sets the position of the media represented by the current instance in its containing album.
member.value: A containing the position of the media represented by the current instance in its containing album or zero if not specified.

remarks.para: This value should be the same as is listed on the album cover and no more than if is non-zero.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.TrackCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of tracks in the album containing the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the number of tracks in the album containing the media represented by the current instance or zero if not specified.

remarks.para: If non-zero, this value should be at least equal to . If is zero, this value should also be zero.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Disc
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of the disc containing the media represented by the current instance in the boxed set.
member.value: A containing the number of the disc containing the media represented by the current instance in the boxed set.

remarks.para: This value should be the same as is number that appears on the disc. For example, if the disc is the first of three, the value should be 1. It should be no more than if is non-zero.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.DiscCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of discs in the boxed set containing the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the number of discs in the boxed set containing the media represented by the current instance or zero if not specified.

remarks.para: If non-zero, this value should be at least equal to . If is zero, this value should also be zero.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Lyrics
member.summary: Gets or sets the lyrics or script of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A object containing the lyrics or script of the media represented by the current instance or if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field contains a plain text representation of the lyrics or scripts with line breaks and whitespace being the only formatting marks.
Some formats support more advances lyrics, like synchronized lyrics, but those must be accessed using format specific implementations.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Grouping
member.summary: Gets or sets the grouping on the album which the media in the current instance belongs to.
member.value: A object containing the grouping on the album which the media in the current instance belongs to or if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field contains a non-physical grouping to which the track belongs. In classical music, this could be a movement. It could also be parts of a series like "Introduction", "Closing Remarks", etc.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.BeatsPerMinute
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of beats per minute in the audio of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the number of beats per minute in the audio of the media represented by the current instance, or zero if not specified.

remarks.para: This field is useful for DJ's who are trying to match songs. It should be calculated from the audio or pulled from a database.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Conductor
member.summary: Gets or sets the conductor or director of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A object containing the conductor or director of the media represented by the current instance or if no value present.

remarks.para: This field is most useful for organizing classical music and movies.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.Copyright
member.summary: Gets or sets the copyright information for the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A object containing the copyright information for the media represented by the current instance or if no value present.

remarks.para: This field should be used for storing copyright information. It may be useful to show this information somewhere in the program while the media is playing.
Players should not support editing this field, but media creation tools should definitely allow modification.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_ArtistId
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Artist ID of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz ArtistID of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the MusicBrainz ArtistID, and is used to uniquely identify a particular Artist of the track.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_ReleaseId
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Release ID of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz ReleaseID of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the MusicBrainz ReleaseID, and is used to uniquely identify a particular Release to which this track belongs.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_ReleaseArtistId
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Release Artist ID of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz ReleaseArtistID of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the MusicBrainz Release ArtistID, and is used to uniquely identify a particular Album Artist credited with the Album.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_TrackId
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Track ID of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz TrackID of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the MusicBrainz TrackID, and is used to uniquely identify a particular track.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_DiscId
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Disc ID of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz DiscID of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the MusicBrainz DiscID, and is used to uniquely identify the particular Released Media associated with this track.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicIpId
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicIP PUID of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicIP PUID of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the MusicIP PUID, and is an acoustic fingerprint identifier. It Identifies what this track "Sounds Like".

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.AmazonId
member.summary: Gets or sets the Amazon ID of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the AmazonID of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the AmazonID, and is used to identify the particular track or album in the Amazon Catalog.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_ReleaseStatus
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Release Status of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz ReleaseStatus of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the MusicBrainz ReleaseStatus, and is used to describes how 'official' a Release is. Common Status are: Official, Promotion, Bootleg, Pseudo-release.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_ReleaseType
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Release Type of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz ReleaseType of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the MusicBrainz ReleaseType, that describes what kind of release a Release is.. Common Status are: Single, Album, EP, Compilation, Soundtrack, SpokenWord, Interview, Audiobook, Live, Remix, and Other. Careful thought must be given when using this field to decide if a particular track "Is a Compilation".

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.MediaFileTags.MusicBrainz_ReleaseCountry
member.summary: Gets or sets the MusicBrainz Release Country of the media represented by the current instance.
member.value: A containing the MusicBrainz ReleaseCountry of the media represented by the current instance or an empty array if no value is present.

remarks.para: This field represents the MusicBrainz ReleaseCountry, that describes the country in which an album was released. Note that the ReleaseCountry of an album is not necessarily the country in which it was produced. The label itself will typically be more relevant. eg, a release on "Foo Records UK" that has "Made in Austria" printed on it, will likely be a UK release.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlFlags
member.remarks: Updated by VisioForge.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlFlags.Absolute
member.summary: The camera supports absolute units for this setting.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlFlags.Relative
member.summary: The camera supports relative controls for this setting. A relative control is divided into a number of steps with no defined units. The absolute size of each step depends on the camera model.

member.name: T:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty
member.remarks: For a given property, a particular device might implement only a subset of the listed range.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Pan
member.summary: Specifies the camera's pan setting, in degrees. Values range from –180 to +180, with the default set to zero. Positive values are clockwise from the origin (the camera rotates clockwise when viewed from above), and negative values are counterclockwise from the origin.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Tilt
member.summary: Specifies the camera's tilt setting, in degrees. Values range from –180 to +180, with the default set to zero. Positive values point the imaging plane up, and negative values point the imaging plane down.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Roll
member.summary: Specifies the camera's roll setting, in degrees. Values range from –180 to +180, with the default set to zero. Positive values cause a clockwise rotation of the camera along the image-viewing axis, and negative values cause a counterclockwise rotation of the camera.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Zoom
member.summary: Specifies the camera's zoom setting, in millimeters. Values range from 10 to 600, and the default is specific to the device.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Exposure
member.summary: Specifies the exposure setting, in log base 2 seconds. In other words, for values less than zero, the exposure time is 1/2n seconds, and for values zero or above, the exposure time is 2n seconds. For example: Value: Seconds: -3 1/8 -2 1/4 -1 1/2 0 1 1 2 2 4

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Iris
member.summary: Specifies the camera's iris setting, in units of f(stop) * 10.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Focus
member.summary: Specifies the camera's focus setting, as the distance to the optimally focused target, in millimeters. The range and default value are specific to the device.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.ScanMode
member.summary: The ScanMode property specifies the scanning mode of the camera sensor. The property value specifies whether interlace mode should be enabled. A value of 0 indicates that the interlace mode is enabled, and a value of 1 indicates that the progressive (or non-interlace) mode is enabled.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.Privacy
member.summary: The Privacy property specifies whether to prevent video from being acquired by the camera sensor. The property value specifies whether privacy mode is enable or disabled. A value of 0 indicates that the camera sensor can capture video images, and a value of 1 indicates that the camera sensor is prevented from capturing video images.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.PanTilt
member.summary: The PanTilt property specifies absolute pan and tilt settings. The property value is a pair of integers that specify a camera's absolute pan and tilt settings. These values are expressed in arc-second units. One arc second is 1/3600 of a degree. Acceptable values range from −180*3600 to +180*3600 arc seconds. If a pan or tilt value is not provided, the default is 0. When making a pan request, specify a positive value to rotate the camera to the right and specify a negative value to rotate the camera to the left. When making a tilt request, a positive value tilts the camera up and a negative value tilts the camera down.
member.remarks: NOT IMPLEMENTED.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.PanRelative
member.summary: The PanRelative property specifies a camera's rotation around the vertical axis. The property value specifies a camera's relative pan setting. The size of the value represents the desired pan speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.TiltRelative
member.summary: The TileRelative property specifies a camera's vertical tilting status. The property value specifies a camera's relative tilt setting. The size of the value represents the desired tilt speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.RollRelative
member.summary: The RollRelative property specifies camera rotation around the image viewing axis. The property value specifies a camera's relative roll setting. The size of the value represents the desired rotation speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.ZoomRelative
member.summary: The ZoomRelative property specifies the zoom status of the camera. The property value specifies a camera's relative zoom setting. The size of the value represents the desired zoom speed; a higher value represents a higher speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.ExposureRelative
member.summary: The ExposureRelative property specifies the electronic shutter speed. The property value specifies a camera's relative exposure setting. Step size is hardware-dependent. To determine the step size, you can make a get request on the Exposure property.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.IrisRelative
member.summary: The IrisRelative property specifies a camera's aperture setting. The property value specifies a camera's relative iris setting. Both the iris step size and the iris step default value are implementation-specific.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.FocusRelative
member.summary: The FocusRelative property specifies the focus setting of the camera. The property value specifies a camera's relative focus setting. The size of the value represents the speed at which the focal point changes; a higher value represents a higher speed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.PanTiltRelative
member.summary: The PanTiltRelative property specifies horizontal or vertical rotation of the camera and can specify both simultaneously.
member.remarks: NOT IMPLEMENTED.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.FocalLength
member.summary: The FocalLength property retrieves focal length information for a camera.] The property value specifies a camera's focal length.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.CameraControlProperty.AutoExposurePriority
member.summary: The AutoExposurePriority (Low light compensation checkbox in a dialog) property specifies whether the device can dynamically vary the frame rate. The property value specifies whether frame rate can be dynamically varied by the device. 0 - frame rate must remain constant. 1 - frame rate can be dynamically varied by the device.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FaceTracking_Single
member.summary: Enable tracking of a single face. This corresponds to the Follow me option in the Logitech Webcam Software settings panel.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FaceTracking_Multiple
member.summary: Enable tracking of multiple faces. This corresponds to the Follow two or more of us option in the Logitech Webcam Software settings panel.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_LED_On
member.summary: The LED is on when the camera is streaming video.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_LED_Off
member.summary: The LED is off, even when the camera is streaming video.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_LED_Blinking
member.summary: The LED is blinking when the camera is streaming video. The frequency of the blinking is determined by the value1, check remarks.
member.remarks: The LED frequency is given in units of 0.1 Hertz. This frequency specifies how often the LED state changes per second. So, for example, a value of 5 (i.e. 0.5 Hertz) corresponds to one state change every two seconds: At t = 0 the LED turns on, at t = 2[s] it turns off, and at t = 4[s] it turns on again. Please note that the precision of the blinking frequency may vary. If the value is 0, the frequency remains unchanged. Use int/Int32 type for this value.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_LED_Auto
member.summary: The LED behavior is controlled by the camera. This typically means that the LED is on when the camera is streaming video and off when it is not streaming video.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Mode_Off
member.summary: Turn off automatic centering of the user’s face when a widescreen video stream is initiated. Turning the feature off automatically performs a reset to the default position. Note that even when the feature is off you can still initiate a manual centering process by specifying the value 2 for the value1 field.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Mode_On
member.summary: Turn on automatic centering of the user’s face when a widescreen video stream is initiated.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Mode_NoChange
member.summary: Do not turn the feature on or off. This value should be used when an action is specified using Reset. Note, however, that specifying a reset action does not prevent you from enabling or disabling the feature at the same time.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Reset_None
member.summary: Do not perform any action. This is typically used when the feature should simply be turned on or off.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Reset_Default
member.summary: Reset the field of view to its default position, which is typically the center.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureVendorAPIValueType.Logitech_FindFace_Reset_Face
member.summary: Re-center the field of view to the current position of the user’s face. Note that for this to work the face tracker must be able to locate the face. If this is not currently possible, the centering process is delayed until the face is locatable again.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.SuppressNoise
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether noise will be suppresed.
member.remarks: The value Gets or sets if additional filtering should be done to suppress standalone noisy pixels by applying 3x3 erosion image processing filter. See KeepObjectsEdges property, if it is required to restore edges of objects, which are not noise. Default value is set to true. Applicable for all detectors.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.KeepObjectsEdges
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether objects edges will be restored after noise suppression.
member.remarks: The value Gets or sets if additional filtering should be done to restore objects edges after noise suppression by applying 3x3 dilatation image processing filter. Default value is set to false. Turning the value on leads to more processing time of video frame. Applicable for Simple Background Modeling Detector and Custom Frame Difference Detector.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.HighlightColor
member.summary: Gets or sets object detection highlight color, used to highlight motion regions.
member.remarks: Default value is set to red color. Applicable for all processors.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.HighlightMotionRegions
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether motion regions will be highlighted.
member.remarks: The property Gets or sets if detected moving objects should be highlighted with rectangle or not. Default value is set to true. Turning the value on leads to additional processing time of video frame. Applicable for Blob Counting Objects processor.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.MinObjectsHeight
member.summary: Gets or sets minimum height of acceptable object.
member.remarks: The property sets minimum height of an object to count and highlight. If objects have smaller height, they are not counted and are not highlighted. Default value is set to 10. Applicable for Blob Counting Objects processor.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.MinObjectsWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets minimum width of acceptable object.
member.remarks: The property sets minimum width of an object to count and highlight. If objects have smaller width, they are not counted and are not highlighted. Default value is set to 10. Applicable for Blob Counting Objects processor.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.GridWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets width of motion grid, [2, 64].
member.remarks: The property Gets or sets motion grid's width - number of grid columns. Default value is set to 16. Applicable for Grid Motion Area processor.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.HighlightMotionGrid
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether motion grid will be highlighted.
member.remarks: The property Gets or sets if motion grid should be highlighted - if cell, which have motion level above the specified value, should be highlighted. Default value is set to true. Turning the value on leads to additional processing time of video frame. Applicable for Grid Motion Area processor.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.VideoProcessing.MotionDetectionExSettings.MotionAmountToHighlight
member.summary: Gets or sets motion amount to highlight cell.
member.remarks: The property Gets or sets motion level threshold for highlighting grid's cells. If motion level of a certain cell is higher than this value, then the cell is highlighted. Default value is set to 0.15. Applicable for Grid Motion Area processor.

member.summary: Gets or sets the influence how fragmented files are produces. Only has any affect when the the 'FragmentDuration' property is set to a value greater than '0'.
member.remarks: Currently, two options exist: "dash-or-mss": for the original fragmented mode that supports dash or mocrosoft smoothstreaming with a single input stream "first-moov-then-finalise" is a fragmented mode that will start with a self-contained 'moov' atom fo the first fragment, then produce fragments.When the file is finalised, the initial 'moov' is invalidated and a new 'moov' is written covering the entire file.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.Output.AudioOutputDeviceInfo.CompareTo(System.Object)
member.summary: Compares the current instance with another object of the same type and returns an integer that indicates whether the current instance precedes, follows, or occurs in the same position in the sort order as the other object.
member.param: An object to compare with this instance.
member.returns:
A value that indicates the relative order of the objects being compared. The return value has these meanings: Value Meaning
Less than zero This instance precedes in the sort order.
Zero This instance occurs in the same position in the sort order as .
Greater than zero This instance follows in the sort order.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Indexed
member.summary: The pixel data contains color-indexed values, which means the values are an index to colors in the system color table, as opposed to individual color values.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Gdi
member.summary: The pixel data contains GDI colors.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Alpha
member.summary: The pixel data contains alpha values that are not premultiplied.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.PAlpha
member.summary: The pixel format contains premultiplied alpha values.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Canonical
member.summary: The default pixel format of 32 bits per pixel. The format specifies 24-bit color depth and an 8-bit alpha channel.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format1bppIndexed
member.summary: Specifies that the pixel format is 1 bit per pixel and that it uses indexed color. The color table therefore has two colors in it.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format4bppIndexed
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 4 bits per pixel, indexed.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format8bppIndexed
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 8 bits per pixel, indexed. The color table therefore has 256 colors in it.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppGrayScale
member.summary: The pixel format is 16 bits per pixel. The color information specifies 65536 shades of gray.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppRgb555
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 16 bits per pixel; 5 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components. The remaining bit is not used.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppRgb565
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 16 bits per pixel; 5 bits are used for the red component, 6 bits are used for the green component, and 5 bits are used for the blue component.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format16bppArgb1555
member.summary: The pixel format is 16 bits per pixel. The color information specifies 32,768 shades of color, of which 5 bits are red, 5 bits are green, 5 bits are blue, and 1 bit is alpha.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format24bppRgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 24 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format32bppRgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 32 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components. The remaining 8 bits are not used.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format32bppArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 32 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format32bppPArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 32 bits per pixel; 8 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components. The red, green, and blue components are premultiplied, according to the alpha component.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format48bppRgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 48 bits per pixel; 16 bits each are used for the red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format64bppArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 64 bits per pixel; 16 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components.

member.name: F:VisioForge.Core.Types.X.PixelFormatX.Format64bppPArgb
member.summary: Specifies that the format is 64 bits per pixel; 16 bits each are used for the alpha, red, green, and blue components. The red, green, and blue components are premultiplied according to the alpha component.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.FFMPEGEXE.X264Settings.Quantizer
member.remarks: The range of the quantizer scale is 0-51: where 0 is lossless, 23 is default, and 51 is worst possible. A lower value is a higher quality and a subjectively sane range is 18-28. Consider 18 to be visually lossless or nearly so: it should look the same or nearly the same as the input but it isn't technically lossless. The range is exponential, so increasing the CRF value +6 is roughly half the bitrate while -6 is roughly twice the bitrate. General usage is to choose the highest CRF value that still provides an acceptable quality. If the output looks good, then try a higher value and if it looks bad then choose a lower value. (FFMPEG docs).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.FLACOutput.MidSideCoding
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether mid-side coding will be used. False by default.
member.remarks: Enable mid-side coding (only for stereo streams). Tends to increase compression by a few percent on average. For each block both the stereo pair and mid-side versions of the block will be encoded, and smallest resulting frame will be stored.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.FLACOutput.AdaptiveMidSideCoding
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether adaptive mid-side coding will be used. False by default.
member.remarks: Enable adaptive mid-side coding (only for stereo streams). Like mid-side coding but the encoder adaptively switches between independent and mid-side coding, which is faster but yields less compression than mid-side coding (which does an exhaustive search).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.FLACOutput.ExhaustiveModelSearch
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether exhaustive model search will be used.
member.remarks: Exhaustive model search (expensive!). Normally the encoder estimates the best model to use and encodes once based on the estimate. With an exhaustive model search, the encoder will generate subframes for every order and use the smallest. If the max LPC order is high this can significantly increase the encode time but can shave off another 0.5%.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.FLACOutput.LPCOrder
member.summary: Gets or sets LPC order. Default value is 8.
member.remarks: Specifies the maximum LPC order. This number must be smaller or = 32. For Subset streams, it must be smaller or = 12 if the sample rate is smaller or = 48kHz. If 0, the encoder will not attempt generic linear prediction, and use only fixed predictors. Using fixed predictors is faster but usually results in files being 5-10% larger.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.FLACOutput.BlockSize
member.summary: Gets or sets block size. Default is 4608.
member.remarks: Specify the block size in samples. Subset streams must use one of 192/576/1152/2304/4608/256/512/1024/2048/4096 (and 8192/16384 if the sample rate is > 48kHz). The reference encoder uses the same block size for the entire stream.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.FLACOutput.Level
member.summary: Gets or sets level. Range is 0 - 8. 0 is fastest compression, 8 is highest compression. Default value is 5.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.FLACOutput.RiceMin
member.summary: Gets or sets rice min. Default value is 3.
member.remarks: Set the [min,]max residual partition order. The min value defaults to 0 if unspecified. By default the encoder uses a single Rice parameter for the subframe's entire residual. With this option, the residual is iteratively partitioned into 2^min# .. 2^max# pieces, each with its own Rice parameter. Higher values of max# yield diminishing returns. The most ang for the buck is usually with -r 2,2 (more for higher block sizes). This usually shaves off about 1.5%. The technique tends to peak out about when blocksize/(2^n)=128. Use -r 0,15 to force the highest degree of optimization.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.FLACOutput.RiceMax
member.summary: Gets or sets rice max. Default value is 3.
member.remarks: Set the [min,]max residual partition order. The min value defaults to 0 if unspecified. By default the encoder uses a single Rice parameter for the subframe's entire residual. With this option, the residual is iteratively partitioned into 2^min# .. 2^max# pieces, each with its own Rice parameter. Higher values of max# yield diminishing returns. The most ang for the buck is usually with -r 2,2 (more for higher block sizes). This usually shaves off about 1.5%. The technique tends to peak out about when blocksize/(2^n)=128. Use -r 0,15 to force the highest degree of optimization.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.MP3Output.ChannelsMode
member.remarks: Joint-stereo is the default mode for stereo files with VBR when -V is more than 4 or fixed bit rates of 160kbs or less. At higher fixed bit rates or higher VBR settings, the default is stereo. Stereo: In this mode, the encoder makes no use of potentially existing correlations between the two input channels. It can, however, negotiate the bit demand between both channel, i.e. give one channel more bits if the other contains silence or needs less bits because of a lower complexity. Joint stereo: In this mode, the encoder will make use of a correlation between both channels. The signal will be matrixed into a sum (“mid”), computed by L+R, and difference (“side”) signal, computed by L-R, and more bits are allocated to the mid channel. This will effectively increase the bandwidth if the signal does not have too much stereo separation, thus giving a significant gain in encoding quality. Using mid/side stereo inappropriately can result in audible compression artifacts. To much switching between mid/side and regular stereo can also sound bad. To determine when to switch to mid/side stereo, MP3 uses a much more sophisticated algorithm than that described in the ISO documentation, and thus is safe to use in joint stereo mode. Dual channels: In this mode, the 2 channels will be totally independently encoded. Each channel will have exactly half of the bit rate. This mode is designed for applications like dual languages encoding (ex: English in one channel and French in the other). Using this encoding mode for regular stereo files will result in a lower quality encoding. Mono: The input will be encoded as a mono signal. If it was a stereo signal, it will be downsampled to mono. The downmix is calculated as the sum of the left and right channel, attenuated by 6 dB.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.MP3Output.CRCProtected
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether MP3 CRC tag enabled.
member.remarks: Adds the cyclic redundancy check (CRC) code in each frame, allowing to detect transmission errors that could occur on the MP3 stream. However, it takes 16 bits per frame that would otherwise be used for encoding, and then will be slightly reduced the sound quality.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.MP3Output.DisableShortBlocks
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether MP3 short blocks disabled.
member.remarks: Encodes all frames using long blocks only. This could increases quality when encoding at very low bitrates, but can produces serious pre-echo artifacts.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.MP3Output.EnableXingVBRTag

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.MP3Output.EncodingQuality
member.summary: Gets or sets MP3 encoding quality.
member.remarks: Bit rate is of course the main influence on quality. The higher the bit rate, the higher the quality. However, for a given bit rate, we have a choice of algorithms to determine the best scale factors and Huffman encoding (noise shaping). 0: Use slowest and best possible version of all algorithms. 0 and 1 are slow and may not produce significantly higher quality. 2: Recommended. 5: Default value. Good speed, reasonable quality. 7: Very fast, ok quality. (psycho acoustics are used for pre-echo and M/S, but no noise shaping is done. 9: Disables almost all algorithms including psy-model. Results as poor quality.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.MP3Output.KeepAllFrequencies
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether all frequiencies will be saved.
member.remarks: Keeps all frequencies. (Disables all filters). MP3 will automatically apply various types of lowpass filters. This is because the high frequency coefficients can take up a lot of bits that would be better used for lower, more important frequencies. This property will disable all lowpass filtering. Not recommended.

member.remarks: Range is 2 - 96.

member.remarks: Range is 2 - 96.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.Complexity
member.remarks: With Speex, it is possible to vary the complexity allowed for the encoder. This is done by controlling how the search is performed with an integer ranging from 1 to 10 in a way that's similar to the -1 to -9 options to gzip and bzip2 compression utilities. For normal use, the noise level at complexity 1 is between 1 and 2 dB higher than at complexity 10, but the CPU requirements for complexity 10 is about 5 times higher than for complexity 1. In practice, the best trade-off is between complexity 2 and 4, though higher settings are often useful when encoding non-speech sounds like DTMF tones. Range is 1 - 10. Default is 3.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.UseDTX
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether DTX enabled.
member.remarks: Discontinuous transmission is an addition to VAD/VBR operation, that allows to stop transmitting completely when the background noise is stationary. In file-based operation, since we cannot just stop writing to the file, only 5 bits are used for such frames (corresponding to 250 bps).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.UseVAD
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether VAD enabled.
member.remarks: When enabled, voice activity detection detects whether the audio being encoded is speech or silence/background noise. VAD is always implicitly activated when encoding in VBR, so the option is only useful in non-VBR operation. In this case, Speex detects non-speech periods and encode them with just enough bits to reproduce the background noise. This is called ``comfort noise generation'' (CNG).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.UseAGC
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether AGC enabled.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.UseDenoise
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether denoise enabled.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.SpeexOutput.Quality
member.remarks: Speex is a lossy codec, which means that it achives compression at the expense of fidelity of the input speech signal. Unlike some other speech codecs, it is possible to control the tradeoff made between quality and bit-rate. The Speex encoding process is controlled most of the time by a quality parameter that ranges from 0 to 10. Default value is 8.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.VLCEXEOutput.Video_H264_Quantizer
member.remarks: The range of the quantizer scale is 0-51: where 0 is lossless, 23 is default, and 51 is worst possible. A lower value is a higher quality and a subjectively sane range is 18-28. Consider 18 to be visually lossless or nearly so: it should look the same or nearly the same as the input but it isn't technically lossless. The range is exponential, so increasing the CRF value +6 is roughly half the bitrate while -6 is roughly twice the bitrate. General usage is to choose the highest CRF value that still provides an acceptable quality. If the output looks good, then try a higher value and if it looks bad then choose a lower value. (FFMPEG docs).

member.summary: Gets or sets video thread count.

member.summary: Gets or sets video end usage mode.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_ErrorResilient
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether error resilient enabled. Error resilient mode indicates to the encoder that it should take measures appropriate for streaming over lossy or noisy links, if possible. Disabled by default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_DropframeThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets dropframe threshold. Temporal resampling allows the codec to "drop" frames as a strategy to meet its target data rate. This can cause temporal discontinuities in the encoded video, which may appear as stuttering during playback. This trade-off is often acceptable, but for many applications is not. It can be disabled in these cases. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer falls below this percentage of fullness, a dropped frame is indicated. Set the threshold to zero (0) to disable this feature. 0 by default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_SpatialResampling_Allowed
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether spatial resampling enabled. Spatial resampling allows the codec to compress a lower resolution version of the frame, which is then upscaled by the encoder to the correct presentation resolution. This increases visual quality at low data rates, at the expense of CPU time on the encoder/decoder.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_SpatialResampling_UpThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets spatial resampling up watermark. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer rises above this percentage of fullness, the encoder will step up to a higher resolution version of the frame.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_SpatialResampling_DownThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets spatial resampling down watermark. This threshold is described as a percentage of the target data buffer. When the data buffer falls below this percentage of fullness, the encoder will step down to a lower resolution version of the frame.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_LagInFrames
member.summary: Gets or sets lag in frame. If set, this value allows the encoder to consume a number of input frames before producing output frames. This allows the encoder to base decisions for the current frame on future frames. This does increase the latency of the encoding pipeline, so it is not appropriate in all situations (ex: realtime encoding). This is a maximum value - the encoder may produce frames sooner than the given limit. Set this value to 0 to disable this feature.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_TokenPartition
member.summary: Gets or sets VP8 token partition mode. This defines VP8 partitioning mode for compressed data, i.e., the number of sub-streams in the bitstream. Used for parallelized decoding. Value 0 = one token partition. Value 1 = two token partitions. Value 2 = four token partitions. Value 3 = eight token partitions.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_MinQuantizer
member.summary: Gets or sets minimum (best quality) quantizer. The quantizer is the most direct control over the quality of the encoded image. The quantizer range is [0, 63].

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_MaxQuantizer
member.summary: Gets or sets maximum (worst quality) quantizer. The quantizer is the most direct control over the quality of the encoded image. The quantizer range is [0, 63].

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_UndershootPct
member.summary: Gets or sets rate control undershoot tolerance. This value, expressed as a percentage of the target bitrate, describes the target bitrate for easier frames, allowing bits to be saved for harder frames. Set to zero to use the codec default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_OvershootPct
member.summary: Gets or sets rate control overshoot tolerance. This value, expressed as a percentage of the target bitrate, describes the maximum allowed bitrate for a given frame. Set to zero to use the codec default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Decoder_Buffer_Size
member.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer size. This value indicates the amount of data that may be buffered by the decoding application. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds). For example, a value of 5000 indicates that the client will buffer (at least) 5000 ms worth of encoded data.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Decoder_Buffer_InitialSize
member.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer initial size. This value indicates the amount of data that will be buffered by the decoding application prior to beginning playback. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Decoder_Buffer_OptimalSize
member.summary: Gets or sets decoder buffer optimal size. This value indicates the amount of data that the encoder should try to maintain in the decoder's buffer. This value is expressed in units of time (milliseconds).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Keyframe_MinInterval
member.summary: Gets or sets keyframe minimum interval. This value, expressed as a number of frames, prevents the encoder from placing a keyframe nearer than MinInterval to the previous keyframe. At least MinInterval frames non-keyframes will be coded before the next keyframe. Set MinInterval equal to MaxInterval for a fixed interval.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Keyframe_MaxInterval
member.summary: Gets or sets keyframe maximum interval. This value, expressed as a number of frames, forces the encoder to code a keyframe if one has not been coded in the last MaxInterval frames. A value of 0 implies all frames will be keyframes. Set MinInterval equal to MaxInterval for a fixed interval.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_AutoAltRef
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether alternate reference frame will be added.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_ARNR_MaxFrames
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of frames to run the temporal filter over. The number of frames has to be less than or equal to lag in frames. The range is [0, 15]. Zero is the default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_ARNR_Strength
member.summary: Gets or sets the relative strength of the blur for the temporal filter. The range is [0, 6]. Zero is the weakest and six is the strongest. Three is the default.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_ARNR_Type
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of blur for the temporal filter. The range is [1, 3]. Value 1 = a backward blur. Value 2 = a forward blur. Value 3 = a center blur (default).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_FixedKeyframeInterval
member.summary: Gets or sets fixed keyframe interval. If keyframe generation at a fixed interval is desired, set keyframe mode to kKeyframeModeDisabled, and set the interval using this method. This is most useful when dealing with a variable frame rate video source when a consistent keyframe interval is desired for streaming purposes.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_CPUUsed
member.summary: Gets or sets encoder complexity control. Changes in this value influences, among others, the encoder's selection of motion estimation methods. Values greater than 0 will increase encoder speed at the expense of quality. See libvpx documentation of the VP8ESETCPUUSED option for further information. Value range is [-16,16]. Values outside the range are ignored. The default value for configuration of libvpx used within webmdshow is 0.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Keyframe_Mode
member.summary: Gets or sets keyframe placement mode. This value indicates whether the encoder should place keyframes at a fixed interval, or determine the optimal placement automatically (as governed by the KeyframeMinInterval and KeyframeMaxInterval).

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_StaticThreshold
member.summary: Gets or sets static macroblock threshold. Sets the threshold for macroblocks to be treated as static by libvpx. When active it allows the encoder to skip blocks that it deems static based on the provided threshold. Values > 1000 not advisable, and any value greater than 0 can cause encoding artifacts due to skipped blocks. Values less than 0 are ignored.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.Types.Output.WebMOutput.Video_Decimate
member.summary: Gets or sets decimate value. Reduces frame rate of input video by discarding video frames based on Decimate value. For Decimate value N, and N >= 2, the VP8 encoder filter encodes only every Nth frame. Decimate values less or equal 1 disable decimation.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.Audio_Effects_DS_Chorus(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSChorusPhase,VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSChorusWaveForm,System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Chorus effect.
member.param: Specifies the delay of the filter (0 - 20.0).
Specifies the depth of the filter (0 - 100.0).
Specifies the feedback of the filter (-99.0 - 99.0).
Specifies the frequency of the filter (0 - 10.0).
Specifies the waveform type of the filter.
Specifies the wet and dry mix (0 - 100.0).
member.remarks: Chorus is a voice-doubling effect created by echoing the original sound with a slight delay and slightly modulating the delay of the echo.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.Audio_Effects_DS_Compressor(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Compressor effect.
member.param: Specifies the attack time in ms (0.01 - 500).
Specifies the gain of the filter (-60.0 - 60.0).
Specifies the pre-delay of the filter (0.0 - 4.0).
Specifies the ratio of the filter (1.0 - 100.0).
Specifies the release time in ms (50.0 - 3000.0).
Specifies the threshold of the filter (-60.0 - 0.0).
member.remarks: Compression is a reduction in the fluctuation of a signal above a certain amplitude.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.Audio_Effects_DS_Distortion(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Distortion effect.
member.param: Specifies the edge of the filter (0.0 - 100.0).
Specifies the gain of the filter (-60.0 - 0).
Specifies the bandwidth of the equalizer (100.0 - 8000.0).
Specifies the center frequency of the distortion equalizer (100.0 - 8000.0).
Specifies the low pass cutoff of the filter (100.0 - 8000.0).
member.remarks: Distortion is achieved by adding harmonics to the signal in such a way that, as the level increases, the top of the waveform becomes squared off or clipped.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.Audio_Effects_DS_Echo(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Int32,System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Echo effect.
member.param: Specifies the feedback of the filter (0 - 100.0).
Specifies the left delay of the filter (1.0 - 2000.0).
Specifies the right delay of the filter (1.0 - 2000.0).
Specifies the wet and dry mix of the filter (0.0 - 100.0).
member.remarks: An echo effect causes sounds to be repeated after a fixed delay, usually at a diminished volume. As the repeated sounds are fed back into the mix, they are repeated again.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.Audio_Effects_DS_Flanger(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Int32,VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSFlangerWaveForm,System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Flanger effect.
member.param: Specifies the delay of the filter (0.0 - 4.0).
Specifies the depth of the filter (0.0 - 100.0).
Specifies the feedback of the filter (-99.0 - 99.0).
Specifies the frequency of the filter (0.0 - 10.0).
Specifies the waveform type of the filter.
Specifies the wet and dry mix of the filter (0.0 - 100.0).
member.remarks: Flange, also called flanger, is an echo effect in which the delay between the original signal and its echo is very short and varies over time. The result is sometimes referred to as a sweeping sound. The term flange originated with the practice of grabbing the flanges of a tape reel to change the speed.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.Audio_Effects_DS_Gargle(System.Int32,System.String,System.Int32,VisioForge.Core.Types.AudioEffects.DSGargleWaveForm)
member.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Gargle effect.
member.param: Specifies the frequency of the gargle filter (1 - 1000).
Specifies the waveform type of the filter.
member.remarks: The gargle effect modulates the amplitude of the signal.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.Audio_Effects_DS_ParamEQ(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS ParamEQ effect.
member.param: Specifies the bandwidth of the equalizer (1.0 - 36.0).
Specifies the center frequency of the equalizer (80.0 - 16000.0).
Specifies the gain of the equalizer (-15.0 - 15.0).
member.remarks: A parametric equalizer amplifies or attenuates signals of a given frequency. Parametric equalizer effects for different pitches can be applied in parallel by setting multiple instances of the effect on the same buffer. In this way, the application can have tone control similar to that provided by a hardware equalizer.

member.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Reverb effect.
member.param: Specifies the decay HF ratio for the filter (0.1 - 2.0, 0.83 by default).
Specifies the decay time for the filter (0.1 - 20.0, 1.49 by default).
Specifies the density value for the filter (0 - 100.0, 100.0 by default).
Specifies the diffusion value for the filter (0 - 100.0, 100.0 by default).
Specifies the HF reference for the filter (20.0 - 20000.0, 5000.0 by default).
Specifies the quality of the filter (0 - 3, 2 by default).
Specifies the reflections value for the filter (-10000 - -1000, -2602 by default).
Specifies the reflections delay for the filter (0.0 - 0.3, 0.007 by default).
Specifies the reverb value for the filter (-10000 - 2000, 200 by default).
Specifies the reverb delay for the filter (0.0 - 0.1, 0.011 by default).
Specifies the room value for the filter (-10000 - 0, -1000 by default).
Specifies the room HF value of the filter (-10000 - 0, -100 by default).
Specifies the room roll off factor for the filter (0.0 - 10.0, 0.0 by default).
member.remarks: Environmental Reverberation filter.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.Audio_Effects_DS_WavesReverb(System.Int32,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Sets the parameters for the DS Waves Reverb effect.
member.param: Specifies the high frequency ratio (0.001 - 0.999, 0.001 by default).
Specifies in-gain of the filter (-96.0 - 0.0, 0.0 by default).
Specifies the reverb mix of the filter (-96.0 - 0.0, 0.0 by default).
Specifies the reverb time of the filter (0.001 - 3000.0, 1000.0 by default).
member.remarks: The waves reverberation effect is intended for use with music. The waves reverberation DirectX Media Object (DMO) is based on the Waves MaxxVerb technology, which is licensed to Microsoft.

member.name: M:VisioForge.Core.VideoCapture.VideoCaptureCore.IP_Camera_NDI_ListSources(System.Boolean,System.String[],System.String[])
member.param: True to list only sources on this PC.
Which groups do you want to search in for sources.

The list of additional IP addresses that exist that we should query for sources on. For instance, if you want to find the sources on a remote machine that is not on your local sub-net then you can put a comma separated list of those IP addresses here and those sources will be available locally even though they are not mDNS discoverable. An example might be "12.0.0.8,13.0.12.8".

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.AForge.VFMJPEGStream.Proxy
member.summary: Gets or sets proxy information for the request.

remarks.para: The local computer or application config file may specify that a default proxy to be used. If the Proxy property is specified, then the proxy settings from the Proxy property overridea the local computer or application config file and the instance will use the proxy settings specified. If no proxy is specified in a config file and the Proxy property is unspecified, the request uses the proxy settings inherited from Internet Explorer on the local computer. If there are no proxy settings in Internet Explorer, the request is sent directly to the server.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.AForge.VFMJPEGStream.HttpUserAgent
member.summary: User agent to specify in HTTP request header.

remarks.para: Some IP cameras check what is the requesting user agent and depending on it they provide video in different formats or do not provide it at all. The property sets the value of user agent string, which is sent to camera in request header.
Default value is set to "Mozilla/5.0". If the value is set to , the user agent string is not sent in request header.

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.AForge.VFMJPEGStream.ForceBasicAuthentication
member.summary: Force using of basic authentication when connecting to the video source.

remarks.para: For some IP cameras (TrendNET IP cameras, for example) using standard .NET's authentication via credentials does not seem to be working (seems like camera does not request for authentication, but expects corresponding headers to be present on connection request). So this property allows to force basic authentication by adding required HTTP headers when request is sent.
Default value is set to .

member.name: P:VisioForge.Core.DirectShow.Classes.DSVLCEXEOutput.VideoH264Quantizer
member.remarks: The range of the quantizer scale is 0-51: where 0 is lossless, 23 is default, and 51 is worst possible. A lower value is a higher quality and a subjectively sane range is 18-28. Consider 18 to be visually lossless or nearly so: it should look the same or nearly the same as the input but it isn't technically lossless. The range is exponential, so increasing the CRF value +6 is roughly half the bitrate while -6 is roughly twice the bitrate. General usage is to choose the highest CRF value that still provides an acceptable quality. If the output looks good, then try a higher value and if it looks bad then choose a lower value. (FFMPEG docs).

member.summary: Gets or sets video thread count.
